blocks: Prototype as thin mise file tasks over the existing Python/RtMidi code. Proposed interfaces: microfreak:episode-capture records selected slots against an episode page; microfreak:episode-rename previews convention-based names, then applies and verifies the selected changes. These tasks are not implemented.

Device name convention suggested by the existing export examples: GitP.YY.MM.DD.A, with the suffix following the episode's recorded patch order. GitP.24.11.23.A fits the 14-character device limit. GitP.2024.11.23.A is too long for device storage but can remain an export filename. Multiple sessions on the same date and suffixes beyond A–Z need an explicit naming rule.

The garden contains historical device names such as Microfreak/Preset/360 TMF.24.11.18.A. Episode links, patch backups and recording timestamps should remain attached to the same patch when its device name changes.

Preserve an episode patch identity independently of its current slot and name. Include the patch's episode order, captured sound fingerprint, original name, current device name, backup location and audio reference. The existing garden sync identifies a preset by slot and name, so note-preserving reconciliation needs extending for this workflow.

Future creative naming: associate a representative audio excerpt with each captured patch, generate candidate names with an audio-capable model, and select a name before applying it to the device. The excerpt's patch association must be recorded; filenames such as mf1 or mf ALL alone do not establish which saved preset produced the audio.

Retain the episode/date identity in garden metadata and export filenames when a creative device name uses the limited display space. Decide whether the preferred device display is the convention-based name, the creative name, or a compact combination before implementing automatic naming.

Audio-model selection and naming quality have not been evaluated. An excerpt records a performance, effects and recording conditions as well as the patch, so suggested names describe the recorded sound rather than proving a unique preset identity.

The local GitP script gitp-tools/gitp_tools/rename_tmf_to_gitp.py currently replaces GitP with GitP in filesystem names and text content. It does not implement a TMF-to-GitP conversion or device communication. It was inspected without execution.

Test against the connected instrument's firmware. The inspected Elektroid connector requires firmware major version 5; this is an implementation constraint, not proof that other versions cannot support the protocol.

Microfreak/UG/04 Presets/02 Save Presets describes name/category editing and saving on the instrument. Microfreak/UG/14 Config/01 Utility & MCC/02 Global documents Mem Protect: Off permits overwrites, Factory Only protects factory presets, and On protects all presets.

Use a backed-up test slot to validate rename, category changes, restoration and initialized-slot handling. Verify the displayed result and persistence after reconnecting or restarting the instrument, as well as unchanged sound data after metadata edits.
Close MIDI Control Center during testing to avoid competing SysEx transactions. The garden reader already recommends this when a response times out.

USB renaming does not require controlling MIDI Control Center's UI. The remaining uncertainty is behavior on the connected instrument, especially category-only writes, resets and active-preset refresh.
On , the connected MicroFreak returned saved preset Microfreak/Preset/397 Imit, named Imit, category Keys, with populated sound data.

MIDI Control Center was open during both read-only transfers. Both completed, with matching headers and sound data and no detected protocol interference. This demonstrates coexistence for these downloads; simultaneous MCC transfers remain untested.
The patch was used in a recent episode. The episode association is unspecified; the capture retains the existing name.
Captured patch files and reports are stored locally under assets/Microfreak-2026-10-03-slot-397-Imit/; the public repository contains the validation notes.
Original raw patch and capture manifest preserve the saved header and complete sound data.
Repeat-read manifest records a second device download whose complete raw content matched the original capture.

Imit preset export (.mfpz) was generated locally from the raw capture using Elektroid's serialized object format and a ZIP member named 0_preset. It was not downloaded through an installed Elektroid executable.

Validation report records the repeated-download comparison and the export's matching sound data. The existing garden parser reopened the export, recovered the name/category and parsed the parameter layout successfully.
Parameter inspection provides named raw parameter values. Display-scale conversions and sound interpretation are outside this validation.
The existing microfreak:download task can capture this populated saved slot directly over USB. It checks response sequence, operation and length for the header and every sound-data packet.
No preset write, rename, program change, restoration or memory-protection change was performed. The experiment read the saved preset rather than the current unsaved edit buffer.

The matching repeat read supports using the captured sound-data fingerprint to detect later changes before renaming. The manifests retain the complete fingerprints rather than relying on the slot name.
Parser round-trip validation establishes that the generated export preserves the captured sound data. Acceptance in MCC and successful device restoration are still untested.
Import the generated .mfpz into an MCC computer bank and verify its displayed metadata, without sending it to the device.
Choose a backed-up test slot for a restore test and compare the restored sound data with the original capture.
Build the reusable episode-capture mise task around the proven download path and validated export format.
Preview a convention-based rename when an episode date and patch order are available, then test the USB write on a backed-up slot.
Microfreak/CLI/Episode patch workflow tracks the broader implementation plan; Microfreak/CLI/Preset metadata over USB records protocol research.

Basic motivation: for , ideally, I'd have the presets used in each episode delivered in and a CDN and referenced from the podcast so people could download them. Indeed, you can see in some episodes, I already do this today. Towards this end, I'd like you to create a new Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth which would represent a single synth preset. The information inside of it should be similar to the kinds of things stored in the preset manager for microfreak as described in Microfreak/UG/04 Presets. does have their own piece of software for interacting with presets on the Microfreak, the Arturia MIDI Control Center, but it's a application and as such it suck my life away like a vampire with all its clicking and dragging. I'd like to have a application that I can reference in a new Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth/Microfreak which would describe how to use it to sync it. At first, I just want to model the preset information, but eventually, I want to also have the binary file stored in as well and keep it relatively in sync with the knowledge garden. The goal is that each entry should reference several presets, for example, Microfreak/Preset/397 Imit would have a description of what that preset is, whether it's custom or factory, and any details about it. Then I - or my agents - can use autocomplete to reference those in the garden logs that document my music improv sessions. The original idea here came from , which aimed to create a CLI called freakio based on and . Ok, so here's what I'm aiming for: either (see also ) or a dedicated CLI which can enable AI agents to keep my Microfreak presets in sync with my knowledge garden's Microfreak/Preset area of the garden without me needing to get too involved. It's okay to download elektroid and use it if that works, or you can make a new repo with a fresh CLI that make a streamlined version of this possible in a reusable way. BTW source code is available to you locally.

in logseq, one can click on a frontmatter item and be taken to a page. For example, preset-on-device is literally the page . I want to develop or work towards a convention that when frontmatter is defined in a logseq entity, then the frontmatter defined and requested by that entity should be related to the entity, for provenance and data definition reasons, and the page for the custom frontmatter attribute must be filled in with its definition - and that definition should be of type Logseq/Entity/Frontmatter/Definition. There's a design tension here. If we click on a certain property, say, preset-on-device, we are taken to a page that is not a subnamespace of Logseq/Entity/Preset/Synth the way that definition page describes. One way around this would be to create Logseq/Entity/Preset/Frontamtter/preset-on-device with an alias of preset-on-device, so that clicking on preset-on-device would take it to the appropriate location in the garden. I think we need to further stipulate that prefixes should have a certain type of namespacing. For example, in the entity system, Logseq/Entity/X/Y/Z/Frontmatter/Fruit should likely lead to frontmatter key x-y-z-fruit. We don't need to do this everywhere just yet, but in this synth preset space, I'd like to do this.

Model: Speech. Type chooses formants or a speech library; Timbre shifts formants; Word scans the selected library’s subset.
Low-pass filter. Saved cutoff: 0.570; resonance: 0.000. Cutoff and resonance are normalized settings, not hertz or instrument display values.
Main envelope: attack 0.000, decay/release 0.559, sustain 0.299. Amp Mod is on, so the main envelope controls loudness.
Cycling Envelope mode: Env. Stored RiseLvl 0.000, FallLvl 0.913, Hold 0.000, Amount 0.953. These are normalized stored fields; rise/fall times in milliseconds remain unverified.
Sample-and-Hold; clock sync on. Stored normalized rate: 0.148; division code: 8. The rate is not a hertz reading, and the musical division has not been converted.
Amounts use the signed normalized range −1…+1. The assignment destinations below resolve the saved Assign columns.
Cycling Envelope → Wave / Type: +0.198. The envelope moves the Speech formant/library selection.
LFO → Timbre: +1.000. Sample-and-Hold steps the speech formants.
ENV → Cutoff: +0.059. The main envelope opens the filter slightly.
PRESSURE → Cutoff: +0.967. Expression strongly opens the filter.
LFO → Assign 1 → Word: −1.000. Sample-and-Hold moves the word/subset selector in the opposite direction.
All other saved matrix amounts are zero.

The expression input mainly changes brightness. The LFO changes both speech timbre and word selection, while the cycling envelope changes the Type selection. These are saved modulation routes; the recording does not establish every knob movement or the global expression mode.

Paraphonic mode is on in the saved export. The PRESSURE matrix row uses pressure or velocity according to the instrument’s global Utility setting; the export does not establish which expression source was used in the session.

Base controls use normalized 0…1 values unless a stored choice code is shown; matrix amounts use −1…+1. These describe saved base settings, before modulation, and are not OLED percentages, hertz or milliseconds.
The saved-parameter inspector preserves the original fields. Oscillator interpretation assumes the documented firmware 5 layout; firmware is not detected from the export.
